pairs.name: FOXBODY
pairs.prompt: Aggressive trap instrumental, 135 BPM, melodic loop, gritty 808 slides, toms, open hats, claps and snares, sparse percussion. No vocals.
pairs.story: This one is a slapper. I cooked it up with my bro Maj from California. This beat even got placed by one of my local friends, who hopped on it in Swiss German.

pairs.name: qoban
pairs.prompt: Dark trap instrumental, 143 BPM, melodic loop, heavy 808s, rolling hi-hats, layered snares and claps, tall percussion. No vocals.
pairs.story: Made this on a trip to Albania. The melody took 10 mins to make. Drums by my bro c0de4n.

pairs.name: salsa farming
pairs.prompt: Hard trap instrumental, 155 BPM, melodic loop with a wide chorus effect, punchy 808 bass, crisp hi-hats and open hats, clap and snare, light percussion. No vocals.
pairs.story: This is solo prod. Felt a dancy vibe that day. My closest friend xpected absolutely bodied that beat when he recorded a track on it.

about: Project question: when listeners can't tell a Suno track from one made by an independent producer, does knowing the human story change what they value, and if so, what does that tell us about authenticity?
This is a creative exploration, not a study. The ratings start a conversation. They don't measure or prove anything.
BPM figures come from each beat's file name and match the tempo measured from the audio. Every clip, human or Suno, is cut from past its opening bars, to keep a producer tag out of the test.

sources.label: Deezer: AI music has surpassed 50% of new music uploads (July 2026)
Deezer/Ipsos survey on AI music, commissioned by Deezer (November 2025)
Newsweek: Who are The Velvet Sundown?

question: Does knowing the human story change what we value? If it does, what does that tell us about authenticity?
hook: At its June 2026 peak, Deezer received about 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks a day, more than half of its new uploads. Source: Deezer, July 2026.
caveat: This is one listening, not a measurement. A change here doesn't prove where authenticity lives, and no change doesn't prove it isn't there.
caveat_room: This is not a scientific result: a few people, one pair, rated twice, and you knew what I was asking. It can't prove where authenticity lives. It gives us something to talk about.
reflection: Did knowing who made a clip change what you valued, or only what you said about it?
If a Suno clip moved you and you then learned where it came from, was the feeling any less real?
If a beat made quickly moves you more than one that took many hours, what does the effort add?
with_ai: Suno: the system this project is about. It generated the three comparison clips from written briefs, so it shapes half of what listeners hear.

Claude: helped refine the idea against the assignment brief, drafted the Suno briefs and project text, cut and loudness-matched the clips with a script, and wrote the code for this page. That shaped the format of the test. I chose the tracks and made the final decisions on what stayed, together with feedback from my lecturer.
